data.narrative:
Noveon Magnetics is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $365M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine private companies and one public comparable in the robotics and manufacturing sector, with primary focus on three same-stage peers: Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $365M total raised as a proxy and applies a typical Series C-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.7x, yielding an implied valuation of $620M. Peer-median analysis across the three same-sector, same-stage comparables produces a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B. This approach reflects observable market pricing for robotics companies at the Series C stage.

Synthesizing both methods yields a triangulated range of $527M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $810M. The stage-progression method anchors the lower end of the distribution, while peer multiples support valuations substantially above recent capital raises. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the three-company peer set and relative product differentiation versus named comparables. The $280M spread between low and high scenarios reflects material variance in how stage-based and peer-relative methods weight Noveon's positioning within its cohort.
